prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment), Main Transformer (abnormal trends escalated), export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; applies Dispatcher ceiling, keeps protection unless authorized). Grid Dispatcher sends external operating requirements→Relay, control personnel. Grid, port out of scope. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus (equipment status for protection/monitoring). Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel (supervises circuits; alarms with location/fault; covers electrical enclosures, machinery spaces), Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; data→Shore Control Room with source timestamps; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; message hub; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Operations Radio Console (voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft), Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation. Vessel Master: read-back; Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. Warehouse System authoritative. Isolation: lock/tag, voltage test; Work Permit Portal current revision, retains decisions/approvals. Control Engineer reviews alarms with SCADA Engineer, verifies restoration. Comms: electrical-safety instructions via authorized channels, confirmed by Substation Operator/Electrical Technician; fallback on outage, report it; urgent messages state asset, hazard, action, issuer; read-back confirmed. Records: originator, recipient, event/recording times, asset, action; facts vs estimates; synced clocks; corrections keep original; Field Supervisor enters promptly; Duty Planner

Document units:
S789: The Turbine Controller initiates the configured shutdown response when a confirmed fire condition requires turbine protection.
S790: The Pitch System moves the blades to the defined safe position when commanded during an emergency shutdown.
S791: The Rotor Brake Unit applies braking only in accordance with the turbine protection sequence and operating limits.
S792: The Converter Cabinet is isolated when fire or overheating threatens electrical equipment or personnel.
S793: The Nacelle Condition Monitor provides condition information that can help distinguish a developing equipment fault from a confirmed fire alarm.
S794: At the Offshore Substation, fire detection and equipment protection are coordinated with electrical isolation procedures.
S795: The Main Transformer is protected by site-specific detection and trip settings that account for its design and operating conditions.
S796: Alarm priorities distinguish immediate danger from supervisory faults that require assessment but do not indicate an active fire.
S797: An alarm is not cleared solely because a detector signal has returned to normal.
S798: The Shore Control Room assesses incoming alarms, confirms the affected asset, and initiates the response appropriate to the reported severity.
S799: The Control Engineer verifies the equipment state and checks that protection actions have completed before authorizing any further operational action.
S800: The SCADA Gateway supports alarm visibility at the shore operating position without replacing local emergency controls.
S801: The Electrical Technician performs local inspection only after the area has been assessed as safe and the required electrical isolations are in place.
S802: A Turbine Lockout prevents remote restart while personnel investigate a fire alarm or complete post-event checks.
S803: The Emergency Generator supports essential functions when normal electrical supplies are unavailable, subject to its designated load priorities.
S804: Offshore personnel follow posted escape routes and muster at the designated assembly point when evacuation is ordered.
S805: The Personnel Tracking Console supports accountability checks for personnel assigned to the affected work area.
S806: The Operations Radio Console provides a coordinated communications channel for response instructions and status reports.
S807: The Vessel Master maintains a safe position and readiness to support personnel recovery when directed by the response lead.
S808: The HSE Officer advises on exposure, evacuation, and re-entry criteria in coordination with the incident response team.
S809: The Field Supervisor confirms work party status and reports unresolved personnel or access concerns to the Shore Control Room.
S810: North Access Scanner validates each presented credential against current access authorization before enabling controlled entry.
S811: The scanner accepts only credentials that can be read reliably and associated with an identifiable person.
